newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Petron H1 net pulls no surprises-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Petron H1 net pulls no surprises-analysts.

text.p: Petron Corp said on Tuesday its net income in the first half of the year jumped 13 percent to 2.25 billion pesos and analysts said the figure was expected despite stiffer competition.

A Reuters poll conducted early this month of seven brokerages showed analysts expected the oil refiner and marketer to post a 2.27 billion peso net profit for the first six months despite a tougher business climate.
Deregulation of the country's oil industry in February had spurred fiercer competition, especially in the commercial and retail sector.
But despite the heightened rivalry, Petron said it still dominates the market with its 40 percent share.
In the first half of the year, Petron said its sales revenues jumped 12.5 percent to 29.4 billion pesos due to higher sales of petrol and diesel fuel.

"Petron's sheer dominance is warding off competition and it will do so in the next couple of years. It will still be a standout in the industry," said Angping & Associates Securities analyst Alexis Cabel.

However, analysts said Petron's earnings in the second half of the year could come under pressure from a sharply weaker peso as the company must pay for crude oil in U.S. dollars and has some dollar-denominated debt, analysts said.

"What I am worried at is that Petron will be hit by the de facto devaluation because of its dollar-denominated loans. Things will be more critical in the second half since we will see how the company will control its rising debt service," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.
Other analysts remained confident the oil refiner was likely to meet full-year net income targets as any increases in cost will be passed on to the public.
A Reuters poll earlier projected Petron's full-year 1997 net at 4.67 billion pesos, up 9.21 percent from 4.24 billion in 1996.
The peso was effectively devalued by the central bank over a week ago on hopes it will end months of speculation caused by Thailand's financial woes.

"We are still sticking to our forecast for 1997. For every peso depreciation, it will mean a 13 to 14-centavo per litre additional increase in cost of sales or about 1.26 billion pesos. But it will not erode Petron's income because it will be passed on," said Cabel.
Petron Corp chairman Monico Jacob earlier said the company was waiting for the peso to stabilise further before making any decision to adjust prices.
Petron shares ended unchanged on Tuesday at 6.10 pesos.
Saudi Arabia's Aramco bought 40 percent of the equity in Petron in 1994 from the government's PNOC, which still owns 40 percent of the firm. The public owns the remaining 20 percent.
